Coloring book · Animal 19

Pulse by Pulse

Help the lion's mane jellyfish cross the cold sea: eat, defend yourself and reach the bay where its babies will be born.

SwimTap PULSE (or tap the water) and the bell pushes the water. If you don't tap, it just floats.
EatWhatever touches its tentacles gets stuck. Swipe up or down to swim far or near.
Defend yourselfSTING the seagull. Stings don't hurt the leatherback turtle: dodge it!
Screen:
Its babies were born!
★★★

The biggestIts bell can be over 6 feet wide and its tentacles can be more than 100 feet long.
No brainIt has no brain, heart or bones: it's almost all water, and it lives in icy seas!
StingersIts tentacles have thousands of tiny stingers to hunt and defend itself.

If you see a jellyfish on the beach, look but don't touch: even when it's stranded, it can still sting.

Real sounds (Wikimedia Commons): herring gull (Marie-Lan Taÿ Pamart, xeno-canto XC488995, CC BY-SA 4.0); leatherback turtle breathing (Philippe Kurlapski, CC BY 2.5). The jellyfish pulse and the sea are soft synthesized sounds: jellyfish make no noise.
